title: EXP-009 — Form Description Recovery Across New Web Designer Client Instance
objective: Create exactly one new User-scope classic BuildFromScratch Form named FX_FormPropertyLab09 using the verified basic-form recipe, record its untouched Form-property baseline, change only its Form-level Description to the literal value `Form Property Description New Designer Client`, ordinary-save once to a demonstrably clean state, close the target Form normally, then close the entire existing Web Designer browser tab/window/client instance without invoking `Unload All Global Form Objects`. From the still-authenticated Web Client, launch a newly rendered Web Designer tab/window/client instance through the supported UI path, reopen the exact same User-scoped Form version, and verify that Description and all recorded comparison properties recover unchanged. The result may establish only UI-level recovery across this new Designer client-instance boundary within the same authenticated Web Client session; it must not be classified as proof of a new server-side Designer session, Forms-database persistence, cache eviction, or IDO-metadata unloading.

acceptance_checks.description: Preflight evidence proves the current editing scope is User and FX_FormPropertyLab09 is absent by exact and case-insensitive Form-name checks before any mutation.

Evidence proves exactly one new User-scope classic BuildFromScratch Form named FX_FormPropertyLab09 was created using the verified basic-form procedure, with no unrelated Form creation or modification.

Before the Description edit, evidence records the untouched baseline for Description, Caption, Version, Device Type, Form Type, Is Master, ScopeType, and ScopeName; Description is empty at this point.

Evidence proves only Form-level Description changed to exactly `Form Property Description New Designer Client`, exactly one ordinary Designer Save completed successfully, Designer returned to a demonstrably clean state, and every comparison property still equals the AC-3 baseline.

Evidence proves FX_FormPropertyLab09 was closed through its ordinary Form-tab close control after the clean Save state. Absence of an unsaved-change prompt is recorded only as corroboration that the Form was clean, not as persistence proof. The record also establishes that `Form > Definition > Unload All Global Form Objects` was not invoked before the client-instance boundary.

Browser evidence proves the existing Web Designer tab/window/client instance was actually closed after the target was already clean and closed, while the authenticated Web Client remained open. No logout, SLO, browser restart, User Preference mutation, or claim of server-side session termination is permitted.

Browser evidence proves a newly launched Web Designer tab/window/client instance was created from the existing authenticated Web Client through a supported UI route, not by direct cold `?MGForm=` navigation. The evidence must distinguish it from merely returning to the previously closed Designer tab/window and must show that FX_FormPropertyLab09 is not already present as an inherited/open Form tab before deliberate reopen. This AC proves only a new Designer client instance, not a new backend or Mongoose web session.

After deliberate reopen in the newly launched Designer client instance, evidence proves the loaded target is the same scoped version by Name=`FX_FormPropertyLab09`, ScopeType=`User`, and ScopeName equal to the AC-3 baseline.

Post-reopen evidence proves Description equals exactly `Form Property Description New Designer Client`, every recorded comparison property equals the AC-3 baseline, and Designer is clean. The allowed classification is recovery across a newly launched Web Designer tab/window/client instance within the same authenticated Web Client session only; the result must not be described as proof of a new server-side Designer session, database persistence, cache eviction, or IDO-metadata unloading.

Final read-only audit proves exactly one FX_FormPropertyLab09 exists, no earlier FX_ artifact was modified, no explicit global-Form-object unload or User Preference Save occurred, and repository changes attributable to the experiment are confined to the EXP-009 record plus evidence/EXP-009/ with no recipe, environment, AGENTS.md, or other-experiment modification.
